stemMd: A glucose molecule is fully oxidised in aerobic respiration. What happens to its six carbon atoms?

options.label: A
options.textMd: They are all incorporated permanently into ATP.

options.label: B
options.textMd: They are released in carbon dioxide.

options.label: D
options.textMd: They become the oxygen atoms of water.

explanationMd: Complete oxidation transfers glucose carbon to carbon dioxide. The released energy is distributed among ATP production and heat, but carbon atoms are conserved rather than converted into energy in ordinary metabolism.

distractorRationale.c: Complete aerobic oxidation differs from lactate fermentation.
distractorRationale.e: Heat is energy, not destroyed carbon atoms.
distractorRationale.a: ATP synthesis does not retain all glucose carbon.
